title: Skatedog
description: Skatedog, as a skatedog preset, is pavement grammar: camera near the deck or the paws, wide lens, asphalt in the foreground, a creature or rider in street sport as a joke. Keep it stupid and low, because standing height is the failure.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Street comedy, animals in human sports, youth: hard sun or sodium night, motion implied, dirty wheels or dirty paws. The gag is the rider who should not be that good at this.
Hero rim turns it into mighty fighter and kills the joke. It is the wrong tool in a court drama, a beauty still, or any shot from adult standing height.
If you cannot smell the pavement, you are too high.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Camera 15 to 40 cm off the ground, 14mm to 24mm, looking along the asphalt. Ground Level axis, lock-off or a short chase that stays low.
Hard noon or street sodium. Subject is rider or animal with the board or the run in frame.
Prompt: Skatedog energy around [Subject], low wide, pavement, a creature or rider in street grammar, joke as sport.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: A cute animal on a board from standing height, or a slide into Mighty Fighter. The tell is sky and no asphalt grain.
Fix it: camera on the ground, wide, pavement, joke as sport.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Skatedog in film?
A low-wide street recipe: camera near pavement, a rider or creature in sport grammar, joke played straight. Height is the look.
Skatedog vs Ground Level
Ground level is the axis. Skatedog is that axis plus street sport as a gag, often an animal or a stupid-low rider. If there is no pavement joke, you only had the height.
When should I use Skatedog?
Street comedy, youth, animals in human sports. Skip courtrooms and hero rims.
How do I prompt Skatedog for AI image or video?
Name camera height in centimeters off asphalt, wide lens, then: Skatedog energy around [Subject], low wide, pavement, a creature or rider in street grammar, joke as sport. Show wheels or paws.
